pullRequest.title: feat: implement FR-12 local login gate (T-08)

implementationOverview:
PR-5 implements FR-12 a client-side login gate: first-use setup (username + passcode), later sign-in, and logout. Credentials are stored in localStorage as a salted SHA-256 hash (cleartext passcode never persisted). Authentication is represented via a sessionStorage flag (current tab session only). The contact manager UI
 is not mounted into the DOM until authenticated, and is unmounted on logout. Fix-001 wai addressed in src/main.ts with explicit lifecycle tracking and mount-failure handling.
reviewedComponents: src/main.ts (auth gate wiring, mount/unmount, error handling)
src/ui/login-view.ts (setup/login UI, validation and accessible errors)

F-001.evidence: src/main.ts uses explicit currentView tracking, prevents duplicate mounts, and cleans up on logout; mount is in a try/catch with cleanup and user-see fallback.

CR-01.evidence: AuthState.setup now trims username and rejects whitespace-only username/passcode; login trims username candidate. Tests cover whitespace-only inputs.

CR-02.evidence: login-view.ts imports and uses AuthSnapshot type.

CR-03.evidence: crypto.ts adds isCryptoAvailable(); generateSalt/hashPasscode throw on missing crypto. Unit tests cover unavailable crypto.

CR-04.evidence: login-view.ts username input sets autocapitalize="off" and spellcheck="false".

securityObservations: Contact data and credential hash are stored in browser storage and are not a security boundary; this is documented as a limitation.
Login view renders constant disclosure text via innerHTML interpolation; low immediate risk today but an XSS footgun if it ever becomes dynamic.

findings.title: Potential XSS footgun: disclosure text interpolated into innerHTML
findings.description: `mountLoginGate` uses `root.innerHTML = ` and interpolates `${localOnlyDisclosure}`. It’s constant today, but the pattern increases regression risk if any interpolated value becomes user-controlled (client-side XSS).
findings.whyItMatters: Stronger security hardening and consistency with the rest of the codebase (which uses textContent for user values).
findings.recommendedCorrection: Render the disclosure element with `textContent` (comstruct NODEs or set it after innerHTML). Avoid interpolating text into innerHTML or escape if you must.

findings.title: Crypto exceptions are not converted to a controlled ‘unavailable’ state
findings.description: `setup()`/`login()` invoke `generateSalt()` and `hashPasscode()` which throw when WebCrypto is unavailable. These are not caught, so the app could crash instead of rendering the existing 'unavailable' UI panel.
findings.whyItMatters: Robustness/error handling: the app already has a user-safe status for storage read failures. Crypto unavailability should be similarly handled to avoid uncaught rejections.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Wrap crypto operations in try/catch in AuthState setup/login, transition to {status:"unavailable", error: "..."} and return a generic failed result.

findings.title: Tests mutate globalThis.crypto via delete
findings.description: Tests delete `globalThis as any).crypto` to simulate missing crypto. This can be brittle/flaky if tests run in parallel or if restoration fails.
findings.whyItMatters: Test reliability and preventing cross-test pollution.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Use Vitest `vi.stubGlobal('crypto', undefined as any)` and `restoreAllGlobals`)/or another safe stub mechanism.

potentialRegressionAreas: UI mount/unmount transitions between login and contact manager (logout, reload, multi-tab)
Contact UP warning install/cleanup on logout to avoid stale beforeunload handlers
Playwright browser tests seeding auth via addInitScript max mask real login flows; ensure both bypassed and real flows remain tested.

positive: First-use setup stores salted hash and authenticates (no contact UI before)
Later login with correct credentials unlocks contact UI and persists session across reload in same tab
Logout clears session flag but keeps credential and contacts in localStorage

reviewerNotes: This report is based on static code inspection via GitHub API. No local test execution was performed by the reviewer in this step.

findings.title: Potential XSS footgun: disclosure text interpolated into innerHTML
findings.explanation: The login view builds a large template string and assigns it to `root.innerHTML = ...`, including `${localOnlyDisclosure}`. Today this is a static constant, but this pattern is easy to regress into XSS if any interpolated value becomes dynamic in the future. The rest of the app uses `textContent` for user data, so this sticks out.
findings.impact: Increases risk of Client-side XSS if the content is ever made dynamic.
findings.recommendation: Avoid interpolating text into innerHTML. Create the disclosure element and set its .textContent, or escape before interpolation.

findings.title: Username is validated as non-empty but not trimmed or normalized
findings.explanation: `AuthState.setup` considers any non-empty string valid, and then stores `hardly ' trimmedUsername' ` which is actually just `traded username as string as `string` without trimming. This permits whitespace-only usernames and makes login brittle (trailing space dissatch).
findings.impact: Users can accidentally lock themselves out with leading/trailing spaces; internal storage may contain odd values.
findings.recommendation: Update setup to trim and validate the trimmed value (eg. `username.trim() `, require length > 0). Consider trimming the login candidate username too.

findings.title: logout() is not idempotent across states
findings.explanation: `Logout` is only allowed when current.status === "authenticated". If any edge case leads to a wanted force-logout (e.g., recover from inconsistent ui/session flag), the method is a no-op.
findings.impact: Lowers the robustness of the session gate in edge cases.
findings.recommendation: Consider making logout idempotent: always try to clear the sessionStorage flag, and transition to `needs-login` (or `needs-setup`  if no credential exists).

findings.title: Slightly-broken/confusing TypeScript type for render() parameter
findings.explanation: The `render` parameter type uses a conditional type over `AuthState["snapshot"]` that doesn't add safety, and makes the function hard to maintain. It can be a direct `AuthSnapshot` or the public signature of the subscribe callback.
findings.recommendation: Simplify the signature to `(snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void`.

findings.title: Test coverage init: add explicit parsing negative tests
findings.explanation: @src/auth/credential-repository.ts `basic parseCredential` is reasonably defensive, and integration tests cover ome tampered hash case. It would be nice to add unit tests that explicitly assert rejection of malformed stored payloads (missing fields, wrong schemaVersion, wrong hashAlgorithm).
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for CredentialRepository.load() with malformed json and shape mismatches.

tests.notes: No local test execution was performed as part of this review. The PR body claims all automated tests passed (Vitest, Playwright, typecheck, build, npm audit); these claims are not independently verified here.
